title: Concurrency velocity emulator for core models (tokens/sec microbench)
creator: Evelyn Chen
description:
Objective: Build and maintain a reproducible, low-noise tokens-per-second microbenchmark ("velocity emulator") that focuses on concurrency characteristics of our core models and surfaces p95 latency regressions and tokens/sec regressions under realistic contention patterns.

Scope:
- A portable harness that can run against hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with identical workloads.
- Workloads: steady-state throughput, interleaved microbursts, ramp-up ramps, and multi-context session mixes (short/long sequences).
- Metrics: tokens/sec per model replica, end-to-end p50/p95/p99 latency, batching distribution, KV-cache hit/miss rates, kernel selection signals, and CPU/GPU utilization.
- Regression detection: sliding-window p95 drift detector with statistical guards (Wilcoxon + bootstrap) and an automated bisect trigger for regressions that exceed configurable severity thresholds.
- Integrations: GitHub actions for nightly baselines, the Console performance dashboard for visualization, and alerting to SLO channels when regressions are detected.

Deliverables:
1) Go-based harness binary with pluggable workload definitions (YAML) and work-stealing worker model for concurrency control.
2) A set of canonical workload YAMLs for our top 6 core models (short-chat, longform, instruction) that vary context lengths and batch sizing.
3) Baseline dataset + artifact storage (S3 path) for nightly comparators and a compact summary JSON produced after each run.
4) An automated p95 drift detector that posts regression PRs with run artifacts and a recommended canary rollback policy.
5) Docs and runbook (Confluence link) for on-call and SRE to execute and interpret runs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Harness can reproduce a stable tokens/sec measurement to within ±3% across 3 identical runs in steady-state for each core model.
- The p95 detector flags regressions with <5% false positive rate on historical backtest (last 12 months).
- Nightly baseline runs are running and storing artifacts in S3; failures create a ticket and post to #perf-alerts.
- Integration test added that validates harness end-to-end against the staging dedicated cluster.

Risks & mitigations:
- Noise from colocated infra: run on isolated dedicated staging pool; include GPU telemetry to correlate.
- Cache-warming variance: include explicit warmup phases and report warm vs cold metrics.
- Model variability across quant configs: pin quantization profile in workload definition and record kernel selection metadata.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: prototype harness binary + single-model steady-state workload. Create canonical YAML schema.
- Week 2: add microburst and multi-session synthetic cohorts, collect KV cache metrics, and implement warmup plumbing.
- Week 3: implement p95 drift detector and nightly job orchestration with GitHub Actions.
- Week 4: baseline runs, backtesting of detector, docs and handoff to SRE/Console for dashboarding.

Observability outputs we will expose:
- summary.json (tokens/sec, latencies, batch histograms)
- perf.trace (lightweight event timeline for request batches and kernel switches)
- perf.metrics (Prometheus-format histogram counters for downstream ingestion)

Notes: This ticket focuses on the harness and statistical regression pipeline; downstream actions (automated rollback, canary rollouts) will be separate tickets once the detector proves reliable.
